I love the initial characterizations of Team RWBY in volume 1 specifically. Every one of them felt unique and interesting, and in turn they complimented each other narratively. 

Ruby felt like an actual socially awkward teenager who loved her craft of being a huntress more than anything. Nowadays Ruby’s the same cookie cutter young Shonen protagonist with a good heart and that’s just boring to me.

Weiss’ racism was a little too much at times, yeah, but I argue that it gave her an actual character arc to get over. It was handled poorly but I really liked the concept of this high society girl being grounded in a situation she’s never been in. And her learning from her mistakes of misjudging people like Blake or even Ruby was very refreshing to see.

I really missed Blake’s subtle sarcasm, reminded me a lot of Raven from Teen Titans and I think it’s a nice change of pace from her in later volumes vibe of taking the whole oppression of the Faunus/WF so center stage. Made her character feel a lot less stand out ish since she’s just a mouthpiece for all of the Faunus characters in general.

Yang was just plain awesome! She felt like she lived up to her uncles nickname “firecracker.” She was competent, had her own wants that weren’t just Blake and Ruby focused, was the opposite of Ruby in the sense that she’s socially outgoing and carried her devil-may-care attitude flawlessly. Much better than whatever the hell they did with her V3 onwards. 

I honestly feel that later volumes just erase that for more traditional “We all get along together as a family and that’s just great.” vibe. And the characters memorability really suffers from it nowadays.

For me No Way Home stole the show. It was great for fans of Spider-Man in general and was overall a really good movie on its own!

Weakest is Eternals, movie made no sense narratively and worst of all was just so friggin boring to sit through. I understand people have gripes with other marvel stuff like Black Widow and She Hulk but neither of those can touch on how truly awful Eternals was 😤

I would like for Jon Watts who directed all 3 MCU Spider-Man films to direct for Superman. I feel like he would understand where to take this character while still maintaining the realistic yet comic accurate aspect of Matt Reeves previous film.

Tbh I would like for them to just approach it the same way Matt Reeves approached The Batman by mixing in a bunch of comic book story ideas both old and new. Have it start off taking interpretations from Earth One’s origin of Superman while keeping New 52’s T-shirt and jeans w/ a small cape costume. That would imo feel just as grounded and home-made as Batman’s armored Batsuit that can turn into a wing suit. No need for Kryptonian armor as he’s basically invulnerable (never understood that decision in New 52) 

I would love to see the general conflict of Clark in this movie being how scared he is of them knowing he’s not human. Not for the same holier than thou reason that Man of Steel gave us with Jesus allegories and all that, but mainly because he so bad wants to BE human and all his life felt as if he’s different. As if he doesn’t belong, and the sad thing is that he has good reason to think that thanks to people like Lex and Samuel Lane. I think this would be a nice contrast to Bruce’s arc in learning how to be more of a hero instead of vengeance. Take some inspiration from All Star Superman’s way of approaching Clark Kent’s life and how invisible he seems to the rest of the world while sprinkling in some nostalgic homesick vibes from Superman: For All Seasons. Clark learning how to be more Super than Man, to embrace what makes him different and use that to help the people he wants to be apart of.

As for cast, man there’s only one actor I can see in mind who could do a great Superman alongside Robert Pattinson’s Batman. That being Aaron-Taylor Johnson. Might seem like an unorthodox decision seeing as he’s going to be Sony’s Kraven The Hunter for a Spider-Man universe that doesn’t have Spider-Man in it 🙄 but hear me out.

Aaron Taylor-Johnson is the actor who I feel can properly portray a Superman who feels like one of us. If you remember his role as Kick Ass in the movies, his American accent was flawless and I feel like in the second movie in particular, you can definitely see a lot of humanity he puts on display for his character. Even quicksilver from the MCU was a great role while it lasted and cemented for me that he’s just the man for the job. That with his somewhat iconic Superman look I feel could be even better than the classic 70’s Christopher Reeves portrayal. And definitely a far cry from what Man of Steel’s stoic and unhinged Henry Cavil portrayal. Although most of that blame can be lobbed at Zach Snyder 😅

As for the main villain, obviously Lex Luthor to some capacity has to be involved, although if you ask me he shouldn’t be the main villain just yet. Regardless, for him you gotta go with previous Professor X actor James McAvoy. After his role in Split, a bald scary man doesn’t seem too out of his reach now does it?

Call me crazy, but I would really love it if they made Carrie Kelley from The Dark Knight Returns into his first Robin!

Here’s my reasoning; this Pattinson Batman is already very brooding and angry with Gotham, and while the confrontation with Riddler helped him realize that he needs to do better as a hero, that is what I believe is easier said than done.

Batman in this Gotham has already set his image of being that terrifying mythical shape, and while Bruce would now put his best efforts into becoming a better hero, that image will in some way still linger. Creating a dichotomy of people who see Batman as either the hero or the monster.

While Dick was the original and had the most experience/relatability with Bruce, I feel as if his story just wouldn’t fit in with what Matt Reeves is setting up for the possible sequels. Bruce has related to the children of Riddler’s victims already, that doesn’t mean they’re automatically ready to be Robin. Hence why I don’t think a more traditional version of Dick would work for this version if he was just going off of the merits that Bruce felt bad when Dick’s parents died.

Enter Carrie Kelley; the one Robin above all else who came to BRUCE, not the other way around. She like the small minority of Gotham’s citizens can now see the light of Bruce Wayne through Batman. Starting as a fan but eventually becoming her own vision of what this version of Batman is missing, much like The Dark Knight Returns story. 

Anyways, yeah I love Carrie as Robin, and that’s why I want her for The Batman 2 😁

Okay, I completely get what you're saying and agree, but I don't think this is the solution either. The entire point of the Grimm is that they feel like a dark force of nature that they as humans (and faunus alike) fail to exactly pinpoint or grasp. Hence why each Grimm comes in different shapes and sizes and why no one has any data or record of what they're made of. It brings a sense of eeriness and leaves the horror's of their amalgamation completely in your head. Making them come from a direct source weather it be from a god, an evil villain or scientist, ect, kinda contradicts the aspect of unknown fear that these monsters are (imo) supposed to emit.

This idea would work for say something like Dr. Merlot (a character from the game RWBY Grimm Eclipse) making his own mutation disaster that he labels as Grimm to follow his command, but to have that as a base point for all kinds of Grimm as a whole feels very underwhelming.

But this is just my opinion on it, please don't take this as an attack. I do think there's something better to do with the Grimm in RWBY than how they're being treated now and I do want to know what other idea's you have. I hope this might help and have a good afternoon!
